text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The high court has allowed the state to include in its appeal against the acquittal of former President Kamuzu Banda, evidence from the 1995 preliminary hearing of a case in which Banda was charged with plotting to murder four politicians.

- The government will not compensate the families of 17 people who suffocated while in police custody last year unless a court orders it to, the assistant chief parliamentary draughtsman Allan Chinula said.
- The Teachers Union of Malawi (TUM) secretary general, Benjamin Ndalama, has been appointed first secretary for Malawi's embassy in Pretoria.
- Over 300 families in Zomba have been left homeless after the Thondwe river flooded its banks at the weekend.

- More than two million kwacha accumulated by the government from last year's fuel price increase and destined for road rehabilitation, is lying untouched because of an absence of parliamentary authority to disburse the funds.
- Lecturers from the University of Malawi, demanding a 50 percent pay rise, have entered a second day of their strike and have threatened to boycott end-of-year exams.
- Domestic workers in the commercial capital Blantyre and administrative capital Lilongwe, are underpaid and receive as little as three dollars a month.
